paper_id: XFMNet_ Decoding Cross-Site and Nonstationary Water Patterns via Stepwise Multimodal Fusion for Long-Term Water Quality Forecasting
title: XFMNet: Decoding Cross-Site and Nonstationary Water Patterns via Stepwise Multimodal Fusion for Long-Term Water Quality Forecasting
motivation: Water quality prediction suffers from complex periodicity and nonstationarity, amplified by spatial heterogeneity across monitoring sites and dynamic environmental factors like rainfall.
problem_framing: Multi-site long-term water quality forecasting integrating heterogeneous time series (sensor) and remote sensing imagery, requiring aligned temporal resolution and cross-modal fusion.
key_insight: Stepwise progressive-recursive fusion with explicit trend-cycle decomposition disentangles multi-scale periodicity and preserves site-specific ecological context from imagery.
method_signature: Multiscale aligned downsampling → LocTrend trend-cycle decomposition → XGateFusion progressive cross-attention → recursive refinement → multi-scale aggregation
evaluation_criteria: MSE and MAE across multiple prediction horizons (96-720 steps) on three real-world datasets (BJ, BTH, Ala) against 12 baseline methods
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Ablation shows removing recursive fusion noticeably degrades performance; replacing XGateFusion with MLP causes substantial accuracy loss, indicating each component is critical.
evidence_for_taste: removing Recursive Fusion noticeably degrades performance
A single fusion step may overlook subtle or evolving features
Stepwise visual integration models spatially uneven and dynamic hydrometeorological impacts
explicitly disentangling complex periodicity and enhancing temporal interpretability
enhancing robustness to nonstationarity and site-specific anomalies
thinking_moves: Empirical pattern analysis drives architectural choices: cross-site periodic coupling identified via periodogram analysis motivates multiscale decomposition design
Nonstationarity and ACF decay patterns from data analysis inform the decision to incorporate remote sensing imagery as ecological context
Criticizes prior work for treating spatial context statically despite rainfall dynamically reshaping upstream-downstream relationships
Identifies specific failure mode (irreversible information loss in one-shot fusion) and designs recursive refinement as targeted fix
